## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A ten-fascicle (10卷) full lemma-by-lemma commentary on the *Śūraṃgamasūtra* ([KR6j0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0118)) by **Ǒuyì Zhìxù** 蕅益智旭 [智旭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%97%AD) (1599 – 1655), the youngest of the late-Míng "Four Great Masters", with editorial review (*cāndìng* 參訂) by **Wēnlíng Dàofǎng** 溫陵道昉 [道昉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E6%98%89). The genre name *wénjù* 文句 ("text-phrases") deliberately echoes the title of Tiāntái Zhìyǐ's *Miàofǎ liánhuá jīng wénjù* 妙法蓮華經文句 (T1718), a classical Tiāntái commentarial format that Zhìxù — himself a self-identified later Tiāntái restorer — reproduces here for the *Lèngyánjīng*. Together with the prefatory *Xuányì* ([KR6j0692](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0692)) it forms Zhìxù's two-part *Lèngyán* commentarial corpus. Preserved as **X13 no. 285** in the *Xùzàngjīng*.

**Abstract**

The *Wénjù* is Zhìxù's full doctrinal-meditative commentary on the *Lèngyánjīng* in 10 fascicles, complementing his shorter prefatory *Xuányì*. Together the two works present the **Tiāntái-revivalist Yogācāra-Tathāgatagarbha synthesis** that is Zhìxù's most distinctive doctrinal contribution. The work explicitly engages with the dominant Wànlì-era *Lèngyán* commentaries — particularly [真鑑](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E9%91%91)'s *Zhèngmài shū* ([KR6j0683](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0683)), [德清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%B7%E6%B8%85)'s *Tōngyì* ([KR6j0687](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0687)), and [傳燈](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%82%B3%E7%87%88)'s *Yuántōng shū* ([KR6j0689](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0689)) — and aims to provide a **synthetic alternative** that reconciles their competing doctrinal frameworks within Zhìxù's broader Tiāntái-Yogācāra programme.

The dating bracket is set to **1635 – 1655**, the productive period of Zhìxù's mature exegetical career.

Zhìxù self-styled as **Gǔ-Wú** 古吳 ("Old Wú") *bodhisattva śrāmaṇera*, and Dàofǎng as **Wēnlíng** 溫陵 *bodhisattva bhikṣu* — the dignified self-identifications signal the work's place in late-Míng *jūshìfójiào* 居士佛教 ("lay Buddhism") sensibility, even though both are formally ordained.
